# Generated by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic)
CRITICAL — Autoware's lidar perception chain runs on intra-process Waitables
============================================================================
Written 2026-08-16. Companion to notes/noticing_waitables.txt (the June
postmortem on Waitables as the 5th executor dispatch category) and
notes/about_docs/autoware_dds_settings.txt (the DDS incident of the same day).

TL;DR
-----
In Autoware logging_simulator, `/pointcloud_container` (one
component_container_mt process) hosts 21 nodes — concatenate_data,
lidar_centerpoint, crop_box_filter, common_ground_filter,
occupancy_grid_map_node, euclidean_cluster, voxel_based_compare_map_filter,
the localization downsample filters, several tf listeners. Every hop between
them is INTRA-PROCESS. Those subscriptions never fire the ordinary
`rclcpp_subscription_callback_added` callback (traced n=0 for all of them);
they are dispatched by the executor as `SubscriptionIntraProcess` Waitables
(branch 5 of Executor::execute_any_executable). Until today those Waitables
had NO init tracepoint, so the whole GPU-relevant perception path in
Autoware was a set of "unknown pointer" dispatches in FISH's model.

Today's intra-process patch (`IntraProcessManager::add_subscription` →
`fish_rclcpp_waitable_init(this, nullptr, nullptr)`, image
autoware-dev-trt-a1000-fishwait4) makes them first-class entities.

Evidence (session fish_20260816_162248, r4, Cyclone RMW, default sysctls)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
pointcloud_container = vpid 1234, procname component_conta

  intra-proc waitables registered in this process : 34
  of which dispatched (appear as callback_start.cb): 20

  callback_start counts per intra-proc Waitable (top 12):
     0x7021746064E0  n=288   } 6 waitables at exactly 288 = number of top-lidar
     0x702154061210  n=288   } frames in sample-rosbag (288 msgs on
     0x7021100D9E00  n=288   } /sensing/lidar/top/velodyne_packets) — the
     0x70214C067F30  n=288   } per-lidar preprocessor hops
     0x70211809EE20  n=288   } (crop_box_self/mirror → distortion →
     0x70212805B370  n=288   }  ring_outlier → before_sync)
     0x7021745EEA00  n=234
     0x702154046A80  n=205
     0x7021540A08C0  n=176
     0x7021200A4B90  n=174
     0x7021200A70D0  n=165
     0x701EC275F1B0  n=162   ← lidar_centerpoint's concatenated/pointcloud
                              input: launch_full.log shows 130 published
                              detections + 32 "Fail to preprocess" = 162.

  Meanwhile the traced rclcpp subscription callbacks:
     lidar_centerpoint  sub /sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud       n=0
     lidar_centerpoint  sub /sensing/lidar/concatenated/pointcloud/cuda  n=0
     crop_box_filter (obstacle_seg) sub concatenated/pointcloud          n=0
     occupancy_grid_map_node        sub concatenated/pointcloud          n=0
     crop_box_filter_measurement_range (localization) sub …            n=0
     rviz2 (separate process, inter-process)                            n=257 ✓

  → inter-process consumers (rviz2) use the ordinary callback; every
    in-container consumer uses the intra-process Waitable path.

Cross-check with the June session (fish_20260629_115617, image -fishwait,
Waitable v1 without the intra-proc patch): 0 fish_rclcpp_waitable_init
events in the whole trace, yet the same container had the same shape. That
is the coverage gap, measured: 100% of the intra-process perception hops
were invisible as entities.

Why it matters for FISH / the paper
-----------------------------------
1. Attribution alone was "fine" (0 dropped — the inner nested
   callback_start carries sub_cb_addr) but the ENTITY layer (L2) was
   missing for every intra-process edge. Task-graph extraction that starts
   from entities would have shown the lidar chain as disconnected F-nodes.
2. The GPU-owning callback (centerpoint inference → 7 737 kernels in r4)
   is reached ONLY through this path. Any "which callback owns these
   kernels" analysis in Autoware depends on the intra-proc Waitable init.
3. Composition (many nodes in one component_container) is the normal
   Autoware / Isaac ROS deployment style, so this is not an edge case; it
   is the main case. Isaac ROS adds NITROS Waitables on top (see
   noticing_waitables.txt) — two different Waitable flavours, both now
   covered.
4. Naive OS-level extraction (sched_switch-based, Abaza et al.) sees one
   thread pool doing "something"; even rclcpp-level tracing without
   Waitable init sees only inter-process edges. Concrete, measurable
   example for the novelty argument (Aug handoff §5).

Model-side handling (postprocess/model_improved_pg.py, identify_entities)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
fish_rclcpp_waitable_init with node_handle == "0x0" is the intra-proc
sentinel. The postprocessor logs "Waitables: skipped N intra-proc
(IntraProcessManager-registered, parent sub entity covers them)" and does
NOT create a standalone Waitable entity — the parent Subscription entity
(from rcl_subscription_init / rclcpp_subscription_init on the same
subscription) is the owner. Verify after ingest of fish_20260816_162248:
  - log line "Waitables: skipped 143 intra-proc"
  - centerpoint's F-node hangs under its sub entity, and the 162 dispatches
    + 7 737 kernels attribute to it
  - still "0 dropped — unknown cb"

Naming the Waitables — RESOLVED 2026-08-16 evening (model-side, no new C++)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Humble's own rclcpp already emits a SECOND `rclcpp_subscription_init` for
every intra-process-enabled subscription: (rcl_handle, SubscriptionIntraProcess*)
right after (rcl_handle, Subscription*), plus
`rclcpp_subscription_callback_added(SubscriptionIntraProcess*, &callback-copy)`.
The pointer in our `fish_rclcpp_waitable_init(…, node_handle=0x0)` is that same
object, so: waitable ptr → rcl handle → topic (rcl_subscription_init) → node.
Verified on fish_20260816_165836: 141/141 distinct ptrs matched, outer
Waitable dispatch count == inner callback count (299/299, centerpoint 220/220).

NEW FINDING — an intra-process-enabled sub has TWO live delivery paths:
  * same-process publisher → executor branch 5 → SubscriptionIntraProcess
    Waitable → its callback COPY (cb ptr A)
  * other-process publisher → DDS → plain Subscription callback (cb ptr B)
Which fires depends only on where the publisher lives. In Autoware r7:
  96 subs fire via branch-5 (e.g. centerpoint ← concat, all per-lidar
     preprocessor hops inside their own containers),
  47 subs fire via DDS (e.g. concat's *_before_sync ← the per-lidar
     containers, velodyne wrapper ← bag, every /clock TimeSource sub),
  40 subs fire BOTH (publishers on both sides).
Consequence for the model: "prefer the intra-proc callback" is WRONG when it
did not fire; the first version of the fix silently bound non-firing
intra-proc copies and pushed 68 publish_links into "dropped — unknown cb"
and 96 firing callbacks into firing_cb_without_F. Fixed rule
(model_improved_pg.identify_callbacks):
  primary F cb  = intra-proc copy IF it fired, else the firing DDS copy
  entity/F attrs: intra_proc_waitable=<ptr>, intra_proc=<primary is branch-5>,
                  intra_proc_capable=true, alt_cb_addrs=[other firing copies]
  cb_to_entity   maps primary + waitable ptr + alt cbs → same entity
  result on r7:  323 pub (0 dropped — unknown cb); firing_cb_without_F 96 → 11
                 (leftovers: /parameter_events of kill-relaunched nodes,
                 hidden transform_listener_impl /tf_static, nodes missing
                 from node_info snapshot — pre-existing, unrelated).
extract_taskset.py / fish_viz_server /api/cb-stats expose intra_proc,
intra_proc_waitable, n_dispatch_waitable per task.

Open follow-ups
---------------
- gantt (/api/gantt) pairs callback_start with the NEXT event on the vtid;
  nested outer(Waitable)/inner(callback) spans mean the outer span is
  currently dropped. A stack-based pairing would show the executor's
  branch-5 dispatch overhead around each intra-proc callback (small but
  real; probe-effect relevant).
- Ingest+model fish_20260816_162248 (r4, GPU-rich, sysctls off) alongside r7
  for the DDS-settings comparison figure.
- The r5 XML regression: not related to the Waitable patch (r5 still emitted
  143 waitable_init); see notes/about_docs/autoware_dds_settings.txt.
